> Seems fixed by adding a sleep before systemd-notify in subshell. Really weird thinking

systemd-notify will generally try to fake the parent process' pid as sender pid. See man page about this:

>  Note that sd_notify() notifications may be attributed to units correctly only if either the sending process is still around at the time PID 1 processes the message, or if the sending process is explicitly runtime-tracked by the service manager. The latter is the case if the service manager originally forked off the process, i.e. on all processes that match NotifyAccess=main or NotifyAccess=exec. Conversely, if an auxiliary process of the unit sends an sd_notify() message and immediately exits, the service manager might not be able to properly attribute the message to the unit, and thus will ignore it, even if NotifyAccess=all is set for it. When --no-block is used, all synchronization for reception of notifications is disabled, and hence the aforementioned race may occur if the invoking process is not the service manager or spawned by the service manager.
>
> Hence, systemd-notify will first attempt to invoke sd_notify() pretending to have the PID of the invoking process. This will only succeed when invoked with sufficient privileges. On failure, it will then fall back to invoking it under its own PID. This behaviour is useful in order that when the tool is invoked from a shell script the shell process — and not the systemd-notify process — appears as sender of the message, which in turn is helpful if the shell process is the main process of a service, due to the limitations of NotifyAccess=all. Use the --pid= switch to tweak this behaviour.

> yeah, as mentioned, if we have the privs to, systemd-notify will make the notification message to come from the ppid of itself, rather than the pid.

The PPID of systemd-notify should be the one of subshell. But here it is the parent shell, i.e. the one manager forked off.

manager -> parent shell -> subshell -> systemd-notify

Oh, so the actual issue is that the description of `systemd-notify --pid=` is

> Inform the service manager about the main PID of the service.

but it also uses the given PID as source PID...

issue_context.title: Want to sd_notify the "real" MAINPID (great-grandchild of ExecStart) to systemd and then make NotifyAccess secure
issue_context.body:
### Component

_No response_

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe

Following the situation described in #25961 I have a daemon started "indirectly" by systemd as the actual payload of a service unit. 

Being neither a direct child nor grandchild of systemd, its PID does not match notification permissions of `NotifyAccess=(main|exec)` so the lax `NotifyAccess=all` has to be used.
* https://access.redhat.com/solutions/3062191 suggests "all" is not secure
* Issue #24516 suggests `NotifyAccess=cgroup` as a safer option for such great-grand-children, but it is not available in current codebase nor in releases

While `sd_notify()` https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/sd_notify.html supports sending `MAINPID=…` I could not confirm that it would also protect the unit from subsequent messages coming from unexpected PIDs (like in that errata).

### Describe the solution you'd like

A special message or additional keyword (e.g. `MAINPID=...\nNOTIFYACCESS=...`) to reset systemd's permissions for the unit from lax to constrained ("main", "exec" or eventually "cgroup"). This would allow services with complex start-up stack of processes, running a single daemon in the end, to benefit from reduced exposure. Note that access like `exec` may be still desirable, e.g. to spawn children that handle notifications as an independent thread to avoid blocking, etc.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

_No response_

### The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for

245
